answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by forcing every identity to post a time-locked collateral bond before its attestations or grades count. A newcomer deposits a jade reserve that stays frozen across several epochs; walking away burns it. When a comet of near-identical accounts arrives together, auditors compare bond age, lock schedules, and voting graphs. Uncorrelated histories pass; a coordinated swarm leaves a trail as plain as footprints on a dune, and those bonds are slashed as a group, so mass-minted identities become expensive waste rather than cheap votes.
